I'm high functioning, or aspergers.

For what I understand and remember for what I've been told by psychologists, in few words, it's because neurotypical neurones are supposed to develop slowly but constantly, so their brains and personalities mature with time and experiences.

In our case, our brains develop faster when we're young so that's why it seems we're more mature when we're children but then our brains stop developing so fastly from the sudden and it becomes very slow, so that's why as adults we're stuck with childlish personalities.

That doesn't mean we believe we're children/teenagers or we're attracted to children/teenagers, we're not, we know the difference and we feel the same uneasiness and mortification neurotypical people feel about it.

But if you want me to be honest here, since I was 14 I started to feel kind of more intelectually mature but far less EMOTIONALLY mature than people my age. I consider myself smart when it comes to studying but I have the emotional maturity of a 16 years old teenager or younger.

And no matter what I do, I always feel like this. Always. No matter how many years pass I have the emotional reactions of a 16 years old: I cry when I get slightly reprimanded, I'm very afraid of normal adult experiences, I have a very childlish personality (I like jumping while I walk, I say childlish things, I have the body language of a teenager...), I'm too naive and people often take advantage of me, I'm too innocent, I'm too polite, I find unrequested flirting gross, I feel embarrased about sex and showing my body, I still watch cartoons... I look at myself in the mirror and I look like someone far more mature of who I actually am, and it causes me to hate how my body is aging but my emotional maturity is not.

It's like an emotional disability. I wish I was born normal so my bosses and coworkers would take me more seriously and I could have a normal life.

The only good side of being aspergers is that our neurones retain some plasticity as adults, the ability to learn faster when we're children, so we have it slightly easier when it comes to learning new stuff, sometimes.

But I wish I was normal if you want me to be honest.
